name: Johneid Newsletter Express
author: johneidplugins

sections.description:
Johneid Newsletter Express is a lightweight, high-performance email subscription and campaign management plugin designed for WordPress. Built with fast AJAX form submissions and seamless delivery engine integrations, it allows you to capture leads without reloading pages and broadcast email newsletters directly from your WordPress admin panel.

Key Features

  • 3 Modern Front-End Form Themes: Choose between Inline Bar, Card Design, and Dark Mode Accent Box styles.
  • AJAX-Powered Subscriptions: Submissions complete instantly without page reloads, complete with an animated loading spinner and dynamic error/success messaging[cite: 6].
  • Domain MX Verification: Validates the user’s email domain MX/A records during sign-up to prevent fake or undeliverable email registrations.
  • Multiple Mail Delivery Providers:
    • Default WordPress Mail (wp_mail)
    • Custom Domain SMTP (cPanel, Google Workspace, Mailtrap, etc.)
    • SendGrid API
    • Mailgun API
    • Postmark API
    • Brevo (Sendinblue) API
  • Subscriber Management: View and remove subscribers directly from the admin dashboard with automated database table checks.
  • Campaign Broadcaster: Draft and dispatch styled HTML email newsletters with template tags like {name} for personalization.
  • SMTP Diagnostics: Integrated test email feature with error-logging transients for easy troubleshooting.

External services

This plugin allows integration with third-party email delivery services (SendGrid, Mailgun, Postmark, and Brevo) to dispatch newsletter campaigns and transactional emails.

  • SendGrid API: Used for sending emails via SendGrid’s cloud mail server when selected as the delivery provider. It transmits recipient email addresses, sender info, subject lines, and message content when a campaign or message is dispatched. Provided by Twilio SendGrid: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.
  • Mailgun API: Used for dispatching outgoing emails when configured by the site administrator. It sends recipient addresses, message headers, and body contents over HTTPS. Provided by Mailgun Technologies: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.
  • Postmark API: Used for transactional and newsletter email delivery. It sends the recipient’s email address, subject, and HTML body contents to Postmark’s servers. Provided by ActiveCampaign, LLC (Postmark): Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.
  • Brevo API: Used for remote SMTP mail relay when selected as the active mail provider. It transmits sender/recipient credentials, subjects, and email html content. Provided by Brevo: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.

Shortcode Usage

Display the subscription form anywhere on your posts, pages, or widgets using the shortcode:

[johneid_newsletter_form]

Available Parameters

  • style: inline (default), card, or dark
  • title: Custom heading text
  • subtitle: Custom sub-heading text

Examples

  • Default Inline Bar:
    [johneid_newsletter_form]

  • Card Theme:
    [johneid_newsletter_form style=”card” title=”Join Our VIP List” subtitle=”Get exclusive weekly tips delivered straight to your inbox.”]

  • Dark Mode Theme:
    [johneid_newsletter_form style=”dark” title=”Subscribe Today” subtitle=”Stay updated with our latest news.”]
sections.installation:
1. Upload the johneid-newsletter-express folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory (or upload the .zip archive via Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin).
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Go to Newsletter Express > Delivery Settings to configure your SMTP or API credentials.
  4. Place the shortcode [johneid_newsletter_form] on any page or post to display the subscription form.
sections.faq:
How do I customize the subscriber name tag in campaigns?

In the newsletter campaign editor, use the {name} tag. It automatically replaces the tag with the subscriber’s name or defaults to “Subscriber” if no name was provided.

Does this plugin send emails via background cron jobs?

Emails are dispatched instantly per submission or campaign run. For large mailing lists (1,000+ subscribers), using an API provider like SendGrid, Mailgun, Brevo, or Postmark is recommended for maximum delivery speeds.

Why are test emails failing?

Navigate to Newsletter Express > Delivery Settings and run a test email. If it fails, an error message block will appear detailing the exact response returned by your SMTP or API server.
